studies.label: TRIZ-C+LLM versus TRIZ-C experiment on engineering problems GT, MB, and WT

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 512), Table 2, Total block; nonparenthesized design-quality values

arms.name: TRIZ-C+LLM
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix supported by an LLM-based AI assistant; a prompt pack covered problem framing, contradiction parameters, inventive principles, solution generation, and a diversity check. Microsoft Copilot with Smart GPT-5 was recommended, but other assistants were permitted. Each student developed and documented a selected idea. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.3.

arms.name: TRIZ-C
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix only, with access to triz40.com and instructions not to use LLM-based AI assistants. Students developed and documented a selected idea. Both arms received the common TRIZ/prompting introduction and practice task. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.3.

studies.task: Each student generated, selected, developed, and documented a concept for one engineering problem: a polymer gear testing rig, a bicycle-drive mounting bracket, or wind turbine power maximization (PDF pp. 3–5, printed pp. 509–511, Sections 3.1–3.3).

ai_tool.name: Microsoft Copilot with the LLM option Smart GPT-5 (recommended); other LLM-based AI assistants were permitted and actual assistant use is not reported
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.3, final paragraph. The paper names the recommended model but does not state its release year.

estimates.outcome: Expert-rated design quality: Method main effect across all engineering problems
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: The final developed solution was assessed by experts holding PhDs in mechanical engineering on a seven-point scale, averaging four criteria: feasibility, requirements, innovativeness, and elaboration. For GT and MB, two independent domain-experienced experts rated the solutions and their scores were averaged per criterion; another independent expert rated WT. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510), Section 3.2.2, and PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), continuation. The paper calls the composite design quality; usefulness follows the reconciled form and the codebook inclusion of creative-output quality and feasibility. Rater blinding and inter-rater reliability are not reported.

sources.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 512), Table 2, Total block; nonparenthesized design-quality values
PDF p. 6 (printed p. 512), Section 4.2, Method main effect of the two-way ANOVA
sources.quote: Regarding the main effect of the Method factor, the following values were obtained: F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076, which is not significant.

estimates.notes: This is the full-sample Method main effect in the Problem-by-Method ANOVA, not a test of the difference between the pooled Total rows of Table 2. The Table 2 marginal means and SDs are preserved in the counts-source quotation for transparency but are deliberately not entered as this test’s arm statistics: problem composition differs between arms, and no adjusted arm levels or signed contrast are printed. Parenthesized table entries are student satisfaction, not expert-rated design quality; only nonparenthesized counts enter this record. The F test supplies participant-level uncertainty because each student contributes one final solution and its averaged expert score; no numerical SE is printed. F alone gives no signed effect. No mean difference, SD, SE, CI, or standardized effect has been calculated. n_units is null because the observations are the people already counted in n_total. The control is coded ai_vs_bau as in the reconciled form because both arms used TRIZ and the treatment added LLM access.

open_items: The paper does not print adjusted arm means, a signed Method contrast, its SE/CI, or a participant-level standardizer matched to the ANOVA main effect. The marginal Table 2 totals must not be used as the arm levels for that test. Participant data or appropriate model output would be needed for a compatible standardized effect; none has been derived here.

The assignment-time total and arm counts are not stated. Table 1 notes that one GT student was excluded for not understanding the problem; whether that student had already been randomized and to which arm are unknown (PDF p. 4, printed p. 510).

The main study remains one S1 experiment, consistent with the reconciled form and the joint ANOVA. Problem-specific contrasts are omitted under the extraction rule excluding subgroups. If the three problem groups are later defined as separate studies/samples, their eligibility and extraction should be reconsidered; no sample redefinition has been made here.

Separate criterion results, especially innovativeness, are not printed. The design-quality composite retains usefulness coding from the reconciled form; alternative construct labels do not supply a separate creativity or novelty effect.

The randomization procedure, study countries, exact assistants actually used, model release year, and preregistration are not reported. Locations in Figure 2 do not identify countries, and affiliations have not been used to infer them.

PDF p. 9 (printed p. 515), Data availability, says data and materials are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. No supplement is referenced or on file for this paper, so the missing numerical details cannot be resolved from the supplied materials.
notes: Read the entire markdown conversion through its final references and checked all PDF pages, including both tables and all figures. The PDF has no appendix or embedded supplement, and c101 has no entry in the supplement manifest. All estimate numbers were verified in the PDF text on PDF p. 6 (printed p. 512); Table 2 and Figure 4 were also visually inspected using in-memory PDF renders. Figure 4 contains self-report means with SE bars, without numerical value labels; no numbers were read from bar heights. The PDF text layer maps the printed plus sign in TRIZ-C+LLM to U+0001; the source quote replaces that control character with the visually confirmed plus sign. No other textual or numerical corrections were made. The main output analysis uses Table 2 design-quality counts, not the smaller survey counts shown in parentheses. Individual assignment is stated in Section 3.2.1, PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510): "Each student solved one problem only and was randomly assigned the method to use". The study is coded lab_rct as in screening because it used a common test protocol; GT and MB were also course tasks. Group/problem allocation was not stated to be randomized. No across-people diversity or after-AI output outcome is reported; the prompt-pack diversity check is an instruction, not a measured outcome. All source-of-record choices were checked against the paper; screening arithmetic and unverified search-record leads were not entered as data.
